value:
R_PPC_EMB_SDA21 (type 109) RELOCATIONS ARE RECORDED AT INSTRUCTION+2 IN OUR OBJECTS AND AT INSTRUCTION+0 IN THE EXTRACTED TARGET OBJECTS. ANY RELOCATION-BINDING CHECK THAT COMPARES RAW r_offset THEREFORE FALSE-NEGATIVES ON EVERY WINDOW CONTAINING ONE. This is an ENCODING convention difference between mwcc's output and dtk's extracted objects, not a code difference, and it is TOTAL rather than statistical.

MEASURED IMAGE-WIDE, both directions, over every function paired between our raw output and the target:
  type 109 (EMB_SDA21): ours 0 at +0 / 14259 at +2 ; target 14265 at +0 / 0 at +2
  type   4 (ADDR16_LO): ours 0 at +0 /  2874 at +2 ; target  2870 at +2, 0 at +0
  type   6 (ADDR16_HA): ours 0 at +0 /  2846 at +2 ; target  2842 at +2, 0 at +0
  type   5            : ours 28 at +2 ; target 28 at +2
  type  10 (REL24)    : ours 11482 at +0 ; target 11482 at +0, exactly equal
So @lo/@ha agree at +2 on both sides and REL24 agrees at +0 on both sides with an exactly equal count; SDA21 is the sole disagreeing type, and it disagrees on 100% of its 14k+ instances. The small residual count deltas in types 4/6/109 (four to six words) are genuine per-function code differences and are not the subject of this law.

WHY IT MATTERS, and it is not academic. claim.law.HV_permute-payload-check-does-not-bind-a-relocation-to-its-atom.20260901.v1 makes relocation binding the deriving agent's obligation, and claim.CN_census-rerun-canary-validated-filter.20260901.v1's FIX 3 implements that obligation as a hard filter inside the order search. That implementation (tools/gdl/composed_census/cn_search.py) compares `trel.get(lo + d*4 + (off-lo)%4) != ident`, i.e. it preserves the raw offset remainder and so compares an ours-side +2 entry against a target-side +2 slot that is always empty for SDA21. CONSEQUENCE, measured: the filter rejects EVERY order over any window holding an SDA21 relocation, and does so silently, as an ordinary 'no admissible order' verdict indistinguishable from a genuine step-0 refusal. The CN pass's negative results on such windows are therefore not sound negatives. This was not a hypothetical: CTriListCollide (game/world/worldcol) was left open by that pass as needing 'a smarter derivation than brute force' for its 20-atom window; its window carries EIGHT SDA21 relocations, and once binding is keyed by the owning instruction the function closes to real 0 (attempt.CH_ctrilistcollide-composed-close.20260901.v1, project matched 63.77% -> 63.84%).

THE FIX, which costs one line: key relocation identity by the OWNING INSTRUCTION, `(off - base) & ~3`, on both sides before comparing (type, symbol). This is encoding-neutral, strictly stronger than comparing raw offsets (it cannot bind two relocations that raw comparison would have separated, because at most one relocation exists per instruction per side in this corpus), and it leaves every previously-derived rule unchanged: all four known-positive canaries (calc_wizard_pos, next_boss_hint, next_legend_hint, ProcessCritter) re-derive to byte-identical orders under it, including ProcessCritter's identity-order case.

SCOPE NOTE. This law is about the CHECK, not about WebFrank's correctness. webfrank.apply_patch's own internal binding check appears to compare raw offsets too - towerRuneNearAudio refuses with 'relocation binding: word +0x18 is relocated in the target but not in our object' on a window whose only relocations are SDA21 - so a derivation that passes an instruction-keyed filter may still be refused by apply_patch for the same artifact. That is a question for the tool's owner (lane WF) and is NOT a licence to bypass the check: a rule must still close to residual 0 through apply_patch before it may be authored. Where apply_patch refuses on this artifact, record the function as blocked on the encoding issue rather than as a genuine non-member.
